// This fixture is source text, not a compiled package: it is stored as .txt so
// the repository's own build never links it. The scanner reads syntax, so the
// file only has to parse.
package sample

import (
	"crypto/ecdsa"
	"crypto/elliptic"
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/rsa"
	"crypto/sha256"
	weak "crypto/md5"
)

func generateSigningKey() (*rsa.PrivateKey, error) {
	return rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
}

func generateSessionKey(bits int) (*rsa.PrivateKey, error) {
	// The size arrives in a variable, so the scanner cannot report it.
	return rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, bits)
}

func generateDeviceKey() (*ecdsa.PrivateKey, error) {
	return ecdsa.GenerateKey(elliptic.P256(), rand.Reader)
}

func digest(payload []byte) [32]byte {
	return sha256.Sum256(payload)
}

// Imported under an alias, which is why the scanner reads imports instead of
// assuming the last path element.
func legacyChecksum(payload []byte) []byte {
	h := weak.New()
	h.Write(payload)
	return h.Sum(nil)
}

// Not cryptography: a variable that merely mentions the word.
var rsaNote = "rsa.GenerateKey is called above"
